title: Passives, quantifiers, question tags and adverb position
matching: Typed answers ignore letter case, extra spaces, apostrophe style and final . ! or ? punctuation. Accents and every other character count. Multiple-choice answers must match exactly.

lessons.title: Recognizing simple present and past passives
lessons.explanation: In a passive sentence the thing that receives the action is the subject. Recognize the present passive by am, is or are plus the past participle: English is spoken here. Recognize the past passive by was or were plus the past participle: The window was broken yesterday. Notices and descriptions often use the passive. By introduces who did it: The book was written by Orwell.

examples.en: The book was written by Orwell.

pt.title: Reconhecendo a voz passiva no presente e no passado simples
pt.explanation: Em uma frase na voz passiva, a coisa que recebe a ação é o sujeito. Reconheça a passiva no presente por am, is ou are mais o particípio passado: English is spoken here. Reconheça a passiva no passado por was ou were mais o particípio passado: The window was broken yesterday. Avisos e descrições costumam usar a voz passiva. By indica quem realizou a ação: The book was written by Orwell.

examples.en: The book was written by Orwell.
examples.pt: O livro foi escrito por Orwell.

lessons.title: Quantifiers with count and non-count nouns
lessons.explanation: Count nouns (apples, books) can be counted; non-count nouns (water, money) cannot. Use many and a few with count nouns: many books, a few apples. Use much and a little with non-count nouns: much water, a little milk. Use a lot of and some with both. In questions and negatives use many and much: How many eggs? How much sugar? There aren't many chairs.

examples.en: There are a few apples on the table.
How much sugar do you want?
We have a lot of time.

pt.title: Quantificadores com substantivos contáveis e incontáveis
pt.explanation: Substantivos contáveis (apples, books) podem ser contados; substantivos incontáveis (water, money) não podem. Use many e a few com contáveis: many books, a few apples. Use much e a little com incontáveis: much water, a little milk. A lot of e some podem ser usados com os dois tipos. Em perguntas e negativas, use many e much: How many eggs? How much sugar? There aren't many chairs.

examples.en: There are a few apples on the table.
examples.pt: Há algumas maçãs sobre a mesa.

We have a lot of time.

lessons.title: Question tags and short answers
lessons.explanation: A question tag is a short question added to a statement to check information. After a positive statement use a negative tag; after a negative statement use a positive tag: You are tired, aren't you? She can't swim, can she? The tag repeats the auxiliary verb. For a short answer repeat the auxiliary: Yes, I am. No, she can't. Do not repeat the whole sentence.

pt.title: Perguntas de confirmação (question tags) e respostas curtas
pt.explanation: Uma pergunta de confirmação (question tag) é uma pergunta curta acrescentada a uma afirmação para confirmar uma informação. Depois de uma afirmação positiva, use uma pergunta de confirmação negativa; depois de uma afirmação negativa, use uma positiva: You are tired, aren't you? She can't swim, can she? A pergunta repete o verbo auxiliar. Em uma resposta curta, repita o auxiliar: Yes, I am. No, she can't. Não repita a frase inteira.

lessons.title: Adverbs of frequency and manner in simple clauses
lessons.explanation: Adverbs of frequency (always, usually, often, sometimes, never) go before the main verb but after be: She often reads. He is always late. Adverbs of manner (quickly, carefully, well) usually go after the verb or after its object: He drives carefully. She speaks English well. Do not put a manner adverb between the verb and its object: not She speaks well English.

pt.title: Advérbios de frequência e de modo em orações simples
pt.explanation: Advérbios de frequência (always, usually, often, sometimes, never) aparecem antes do verbo principal e depois de be: She often reads. He is always late. Advérbios de modo (quickly, carefully, well) normalmente aparecem depois do verbo ou do objeto: He drives carefully. She speaks English well. Não coloque um advérbio de modo entre o verbo e seu objeto: não diga She speaks well English.
